title: Fullness of Worth
note: This is being full of many good qualities and ruling them. It gathers the many qualities that don’t fall under greatness, so it follows that chapter.

couplets.plain: They say every good thing is a duty for those who know what is due and take up worth.
couplets.pm: The books say that for those who know what befits them and live by worth, all good qualities are simply natural. If some were missing, or were put on by effort, the word for this quality wouldn’t apply.
couplets.note: கடன் usually means duty, and the plain reading keeps that. He takes it here as what is natural: good qualities aren’t a duty for such people but their nature.

links.quote: every good thing is a duty
links.reason: Once someone takes up worth, every good thing becomes a duty.

couplets.plain: The goodness of the worthy is goodness of character. No other goodness counts as goodness at all.
couplets.pm: The good of the worthy is the good that comes from their qualities. The other kind, the good of the body’s limbs, isn’t among good things at all, because it has no place in the list the books give, beginning with birth and learning.

links.quote: The goodness of the worthy is goodness of character
links.reason: Finds the only real goodness of the worthy in their character and none anywhere else.

couplets.plain: Loving-kindness, a sense of shame, helpfulness, considerateness and truthfulness are the five pillars that hold up worth.
couplets.pm: Loving-kindness for others as well as your own people, shame at blame and sin, helpfulness to everyone, kind regard for old friends, and truth in every place: these five pillars bear the load of worth. They are called pillars because without them worth can’t stand.

links.quote: the five pillars that hold up worth
links.reason: Names the five pillars that hold up worth.

links.quote: Loving-kindness
links.reason: First of the five is loving-kindness.

links.quote: a sense of shame
helpfulness
links.reason: Helpfulness, the readiness to be of use, stands third.

links.quote: considerateness
links.reason: Fourth is considerateness, the kindly eye towards other people.

links.quote: truthfulness
links.reason: Truthfulness closes the list as the fifth pillar.

couplets.plain: The good of penance lies in not killing. The good of worth lies in not speaking of others’ wrongs.
couplets.pm: Penance needs other virtues too, but it rests above all on the virtue of killing no living thing. In the same way worth needs other qualities too, but it rests above all on the quality of not speaking of others’ faults.

links.quote: The good of worth lies in not speaking of others’ wrongs
links.reason: Makes not speaking of others’ wrongs the mark of worth, as not killing marks penance.

links.quote: not speaking of others’ wrongs
links.reason: Others’ wrongs are the one thing a person of worth above all won’t talk about.

links.quote: The good of penance lies in not killing
links.reason: Gives penance a single defining good, that of not killing.

couplets.plain: The strength of the capable is bowing. That is the weapon the worthy use to turn enemies around.
couplets.pm: The strength of those who finish a task is to humble themselves and win over the people who can help with it. That is also the tool by which the worthy end the enmity of their foes. He praises the humility that suits worth, and names the other use along with it.

links.quote: The strength of the capable is bowing
links.reason: Turns the usual idea round: bowing is what strength consists of, and a weapon against enemies.

couplets.plain: What is the touchstone of worth? Accepting defeat, even from those who are not your equals.
couplets.pm: What is the touchstone that tests the gold of worth? Taking from your inferiors too the defeat you would take from your betters. You could win, but you accept it. Worth is measured when you don’t make yourself their equal by trying to beat them, and so stand above them through defeat.

links.quote: Accepting defeat, even from those who are not your equals
links.reason: Sets the test: accepting defeat even from those who are not your equals.

links.quote: What is the touchstone of worth?

couplets.plain: What use is worth, if you don’t do kindness even to those who have done you harm?
couplets.pm: If the worthy don’t do pleasant things even for those who have done them unpleasant things, what other use does their worth have? If they also do harm in return, their worth is of no use at all.
couplets.sensitive: urges doing good to those who harm you

links.quote: do kindness even to those who have done you harm
What use is worth
links.reason: Asks what use worth has if kindness stops at those who hurt you.

couplets.plain: Having nothing is no disgrace, if you have the strength called worth.
couplets.pm: Poverty is no disgrace to someone who has the strength called worth. It is called strength because it keeps you from weakening. “Poverty” stands for what poverty brings. The worthy stand above others even when they are poor.

links.quote: if you have the strength called worth
links.reason: The strength of worth is enough to lift the shame from having nothing.

links.remove: The Tamil calls worth a strength, not wealth. The treasure image came from the old English.

links.quote: Having nothing is no disgrace

couplets.plain: Even if the age itself shifts, those called the ocean of worth will not shift.
couplets.pm: They are called the shore of the sea of worth. Even if, as the age turns, the ordinary sea leaves its shore, they will not change. Worth is made a sea to show how great it is, and those who have it are its shore because they hold it in.
couplets.note: ஆழி can mean the sea or its shore. The plain reading takes the sea. He takes the shore: worth is the sea, and these people are what holds it.

links.quote: those called the ocean of worth will not shift
links.reason: Those called the ocean of worth hold firm even when the age itself shifts.

couplets.plain: If the worthy fall from their worth, even the great earth can’t bear its load.
couplets.pm: If those full of many qualities fall from their nature, the great earth too will fail to bear its load. But it is their nature not to fall and the earth’s to bear, so neither will ever happen. Some say the earth bears its load with the worthy as its helpers, so without them it couldn’t.

links.quote: If the worthy fall from their worth
links.reason: Makes the worth of the worthy what the earth’s bearing of its load depends on.

links.quote: even the great earth can’t bear its load

ideaLinks.reason: Loving-kindness is the first of the five pillars that hold up worth.
Take away the readiness to be of use, and one pillar of worth is gone.
Worth leans on a kindly eye towards other people.
The last pillar named under worth is truthfulness.
Shame is a pillar of worth in 983, and in 1013 the good that worth is tied to.
